summary: Jeff Dolven studied at Oxford and earned his PhD in English from Yale. He held posts at Brandeis, the Harvard Society of Fellows, and Trinity College, Cambridge, and became professor of English at Princeton in 1999.

Philosopher Jeff Malpas earned a BA at the University of Auckland and a PhD at the Australian National University. His career included posts at Murdoch University, the University of New England, and the University of Tasmania, where he became Emeritus Distinguished Professor.
Specializing in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology, Jeff Watt studied under Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima and held a post at the Rubin Museum of Art.
Jeff Wilson works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and studied under mentors Taitetsu Unno and Akio Tatsuguchi.

Working in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy, Jeffery D. Long studied at the University of Notre Dame and earned an MA and PhD from the University of Chicago Divinity School. In 2000, he joined Elizabethtown College as Associate Professor.

Jeffrey Broughton, a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology, earned his PhD from Columbia University in 1975. By 2004, he was a professor in the Department of Religious Studies at California State University.

Jeffrey Clark Ruff studied at Missouri State University and the University of California, Santa Barbara, completing his PhD under David Gordon White. A scholar of Indology and religious studies, he became Assistant Professor at Marshall University in 2002.

Jeffrey Hopkins was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, among others. From 1973 to 2005, he served as Associate Professor and center director at the University of Virginia.

Specializing in religious studies and Indology, Jeffrey J. Kripal studied at Conception Seminary College and earned his PhD from the University of Chicago. Around 2002, he was appointed J. Newton Rayzor Chair and department chair at Rice University.

Jeffrey K. Riegel is a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He served as Professor of Chinese at the University of California, Berkeley from 1979 to 2007, and subsequently held a post at the University of Sydney from 2007 to 2017.

Jeffrey Kotyk specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He earned an MA at Komazawa University and a PhD from Leiden University under James A. Benn, later holding posts at McMaster University and the University of Bologna.

Working in French literature and philosophy, Jeffrey Mehlman held positions at Cornell, Yale, and Johns Hopkins. Around 1983, he became University Professor and Professor of French Literature at Boston University.

Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard, earning his PhD in 1970. A scholar of Indology and philosophy, he taught at the University of Toronto (1969–1980) and UC Berkeley as Professor of Sanskrit (1981–1992).

Jeffrey Newmark, a scholar of Japanology, history, and archaeology, completed studies at Harvard University (circa 1994–1996) and the University of British Columbia (circa 2002–2009). He held a post at the University of Winnipeg around 2011.
Jeffrey S. Lidke is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He held a post at Berry College and was attested as a visiting assistant professor of religion at the University of Virginia in 2003.

Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, Jeffrey Samuels earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Karen Christina Lang and studied under W. S. Karunatillake. By 2013, he was Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Western Kentucky University.

Jeffrey Schoening is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 1991), where he was supervised by Collett Cox and advised by Sanghasen Singh.

Jeffrey Stout studied at Brown University and earned his PhD at Princeton University. A scholar of religious studies and philosophy, he served as a professor at Princeton University from 1976 to 2018.

Jeffrey Wayne Bass studied at UNC Wilmington, the University of Tennessee, and earned his PhD at UCLA under Gregory Schopen. A scholar in Buddhist studies, he has held teaching posts at UCLA and UC San Diego.

Jenkuan Shih is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a master's under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the doctoral supervision of Charles Hallisey and Mark Csikszentmihalyi.
